# o2pg conversion rule reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_rules_doc.py from the conversion registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

`o2pg convert` applies 53 mechanical rewrites and knows 44 kinds of review point. Every rewrite it makes is counted in the conversion report. Every review point is left in the output as `/* O2PG-REVIEW <rule>: <reason> */` on the line above the code. Blocking review points mark Oracle code that will not work as written; it is left in place on purpose, so the routine fails to compile instead of running with the wrong behaviour.

## Rewrites

### O2PG-CV-001: Routine header

`[CREATE OR REPLACE] PROCEDURE|FUNCTION name (...) IS|AS` becomes `CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE|FUNCTION schema.name (...) LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ ... $$;`. The declarations between IS/AS and BEGIN move under `DECLARE`.

### O2PG-CV-002: Function RETURN clause

`RETURN type` in a function header becomes `RETURNS type`.

### O2PG-CV-003: Parameter modes

`p IN t`, `p OUT t` and `p IN OUT [NOCOPY] t` become `p t`, `OUT p t` and `INOUT p t`. PostgreSQL writes the mode before the name.

### O2PG-CV-004: Data types

Parameter, return, variable and `CAST` types are mapped with the same table as `o2pg map-types` (`VARCHAR2(n)` to `varchar(n)`, `NUMBER(p,s)` to `numeric(p,s)`, `DATE` to `timestamp(0)`, `CLOB` to `text`, ...). PL/SQL-only types map to `integer` (`PLS_INTEGER`, `BINARY_INTEGER`, `NATURAL`, `POSITIVE`), `boolean` and `refcursor` (`SYS_REFCURSOR`). `%TYPE` and `%ROWTYPE` are kept: PL/pgSQL supports both.

**Check:** Oracle INTEGER and SMALLINT are NUMBER(38) and are kept as PostgreSQL integer and smallint, which raise an error on overflow; widen them to numeric if values can exceed the 32-bit or 16-bit range.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-DT-001, O2PG-DT-003.

### O2PG-CV-005: Parameter defaults

`p t := expr` and `p t DEFAULT expr` in a parameter list become `p t DEFAULT expr`.

### O2PG-CV-006: END labels

`END name;` becomes `END;` when no `<<name>>` label exists. PL/pgSQL only accepts a name after END when it matches a block label.

### O2PG-CV-007: search_path pinned on the routine

Converted routines get `SET search_path = <owner schema>, public` (package routines also get the package schema first), because Oracle resolves unqualified names in the owner's schema. The file also sets search_path before the CREATE so `%TYPE` references resolve.

**Check:** A procedure that commits or rolls back cannot carry a SET clause in PostgreSQL, so those procedures are left without it and resolve names through the caller's search_path.

### O2PG-CV-008: Invoker and definer rights

`AUTHID CURRENT_USER` becomes `SECURITY INVOKER`. Oracle's default (definer rights) is not copied: the routine runs with the caller's privileges, which is PostgreSQL's default.

**Check:** Oracle runs this code with the owner's privileges by default. Grant callers what they need, or add SECURITY DEFINER deliberately (keep the SET search_path if you do).

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SE-004.

### O2PG-CV-009: Oracle-only routine options

`DETERMINISTIC`, `RESULT_CACHE`, `PARALLEL_ENABLE` and `ACCESSIBLE BY` are kept as a comment on the routine. None of them changes results.

**Check:** PostgreSQL routines default to VOLATILE. Mark them IMMUTABLE or STABLE yourself once you know they do not read changing data.

### O2PG-CV-010: Explicit cursor declarations

`CURSOR c (p NUMBER) IS SELECT ...` becomes `c CURSOR (p numeric) FOR SELECT ...`.

### O2PG-CV-011: REF CURSOR types

`TYPE t IS REF CURSOR [RETURN ...]` is kept as a comment and every use of `t` becomes `refcursor`.

**Check:** The RETURN row type of a strong REF CURSOR is not enforced by refcursor.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-005.

### O2PG-CV-012: Package split into a schema

A package becomes a schema named after the package, with one PostgreSQL routine per procedure or function in the package body.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-001.

### O2PG-CV-013: Package constants inlined

Package-level `CONSTANT` declarations are copied into the DECLARE section of each routine that uses them.

### O2PG-CV-014: Forward declarations

Forward declarations in a package body are kept as comments; PL/pgSQL does not need them.

### O2PG-CV-015: NVL to COALESCE

`NVL(a, b)` becomes `COALESCE(a, b)`.

**Check:** NVL converts b to the type of a; COALESCE needs a common type, so NVL(number, 'text') style calls fail and need an explicit cast.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-004.

### O2PG-CV-016: NVL2 to CASE

`NVL2(a, b, c)` becomes `CASE WHEN a IS NOT NULL THEN b ELSE c END`.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-004.

### O2PG-CV-017: DECODE to CASE

`DECODE(x, s1, r1, ..., default)` becomes `CASE x WHEN s1 THEN r1 ... ELSE default END` when every search value is a non-NULL literal. When a search value is `NULL`, `''` or an expression, and x is a simple name, it becomes a searched CASE using `IS NULL` or `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`, because DECODE treats two NULLs as equal.

**Check:** DECODE converts every result to the type of the first one; CASE needs compatible types.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-003.

### O2PG-CV-018: SYSDATE and CURRENT_DATE

`SYSDATE` and Oracle's `CURRENT_DATE` become `LOCALTIMESTAMP(0)`, the same choice `o2pg map-types` makes for column defaults.

**Check:** LOCALTIMESTAMP is fixed at the start of the transaction; SYSDATE reads the clock on every call and uses the database server's time zone. Use clock_timestamp()::timestamp(0) where code measures elapsed time inside one transaction.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-007.

### O2PG-CV-019: SYSTIMESTAMP

`SYSTIMESTAMP` becomes `clock_timestamp()`, which also reads the clock on every call and returns a time zone aware value.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-007.

### O2PG-CV-020: Sequence NEXTVAL and CURRVAL

`seq.NEXTVAL` becomes `nextval('seq')` and `seq.CURRVAL` becomes `currval('seq')`, with the same identifier folding as `o2pg map-types`.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-014.

### O2PG-CV-021: FROM DUAL

`FROM DUAL` is removed. PostgreSQL allows SELECT without FROM.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-009.

### O2PG-CV-022: SELECT expr INTO var without FROM

`SELECT expr INTO target;` with a single expression and no FROM (usually after FROM DUAL is removed) becomes `target := expr;`.

### O2PG-CV-023: SELECT INTO STRICT

`SELECT ... INTO target FROM ...` and `EXECUTE ... INTO target` get `STRICT`, so a query that returns no rows raises `no_data_found` and one that returns several raises `too_many_rows`, as in Oracle. Without STRICT, PostgreSQL silently stores NULL or the first row.

**Check:** This restores Oracle's behaviour; check that exception handlers expect it. Aggregates without GROUP BY always return one row, so STRICT changes nothing there.

### O2PG-CV-024: DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE

`DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(x);` becomes `RAISE NOTICE '%', x;`.

**Check:** Notices go to the client and the server log (depending on log_min_messages).

### O2PG-CV-025: RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR

`RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20001, msg)` becomes `RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'P0001', MESSAGE = msg, HINT = 'Oracle error code -20001'`.

**Check:** Callers that test SQLCODE for the -20xxx number must test SQLSTATE 'P0001' and the message or hint instead.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-013.

### O2PG-CV-026: Predefined exception names

`DUP_VAL_ON_INDEX` becomes `unique_violation`, `ZERO_DIVIDE` becomes `division_by_zero`, `INVALID_NUMBER` becomes `invalid_text_representation`, `VALUE_ERROR` becomes `data_exception`, `CURSOR_ALREADY_OPEN` becomes `duplicate_cursor`, `INVALID_CURSOR` becomes `invalid_cursor_state` and `TIMEOUT_ON_RESOURCE` becomes `lock_not_available`. `NO_DATA_FOUND`, `TOO_MANY_ROWS` and `OTHERS` exist in PL/pgSQL under the same names.

**Check:** VALUE_ERROR maps to the whole data_exception class, which is slightly wider.

### O2PG-CV-027: SQLCODE to SQLSTATE

`SQLCODE` becomes `SQLSTATE`. Also flagged for review because the value changes from a negative number to a five-character code.

### O2PG-CV-028: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE

`EXECUTE IMMEDIATE str` becomes `EXECUTE str`. Also flagged for review because the SQL text itself is not converted.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-007.

### O2PG-CV-029: COMMIT and ROLLBACK in procedures

Transaction control in a procedure is kept: PostgreSQL 11+ procedures can COMMIT and ROLLBACK.

**Check:** Such a procedure must be called with CALL outside an explicit transaction block, not from a function or trigger, and cannot commit inside a BEGIN ... EXCEPTION block. It is also created without SET search_path (see O2PG-CV-007).

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-014.

### O2PG-CV-030: :NEW and :OLD

`:NEW.col` and `:OLD.col` (and REFERENCING aliases) become `NEW.col` and `OLD.col`.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-OB-004.

### O2PG-CV-031: INSERTING, UPDATING, DELETING

`INSERTING`, `UPDATING` and `DELETING` become `(TG_OP = 'INSERT')`, `(TG_OP = 'UPDATE')` and `(TG_OP = 'DELETE')`.

### O2PG-CV-032: Row and statement triggers

A simple BEFORE/AFTER/INSTEAD OF trigger becomes a `RETURNS trigger` function that wraps the Oracle block and returns `NEW` (BEFORE/INSTEAD OF row triggers; `OLD` for DELETE) or `NULL`, followed by `CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER ... EXECUTE FUNCTION`. The WHEN clause, `UPDATE OF` column lists and FOR EACH ROW carry over.

**Check:** CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER needs PostgreSQL 14 or later.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-OB-004.

### O2PG-CV-033: Cursor FOR loop records

`FOR r IN (SELECT ...) LOOP` is kept; PL/pgSQL needs the loop variable declared, so `r record;` is added to the DECLARE section.

### O2PG-CV-034: FOR ... IN REVERSE bounds

`FOR i IN REVERSE 1 .. n` becomes `FOR i IN REVERSE n .. 1`; PL/pgSQL expects the upper bound first. A short comment marks the swap so a second run leaves it alone.

### O2PG-CV-035: Cursor attributes

`SQL%FOUND` and `c%FOUND` become `FOUND`, `%NOTFOUND` becomes `NOT FOUND`, `SQL%ISOPEN` becomes `false`, and `v := SQL%ROWCOUNT;` becomes `GET DIAGNOSTICS v = ROW_COUNT;`.

**Check:** FOUND reflects the most recent statement, so c%NOTFOUND is only equivalent directly after FETCH c, which is the usual pattern.

### O2PG-CV-036: Procedure call statements

A statement that is only a call, `proc(args);` or `pkg.proc;`, becomes `CALL proc(args);`. In Oracle such a statement can only be a procedure call.

### O2PG-CV-037: TRUNC on dates

`TRUNC(d)` and `TRUNC(d, 'MM')` become `date_trunc('day', d)` and `date_trunc('month', d)` when d is SYSDATE, SYSTIMESTAMP or a variable declared as a date or timestamp.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-011.

### O2PG-CV-038: ADD_MONTHS

`ADD_MONTHS(d, n)` becomes `(d + interval '1 month' * (n))`.

**Check:** ADD_MONTHS moves the last day of a month to the last day of the target month (28 Feb + 1 month = 31 Mar); interval arithmetic gives 28 Mar.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-011.

### O2PG-CV-039: Date plus or minus a number

`d + n` and `d - n`, where d is SYSDATE, SYSTIMESTAMP, a converted TRUNC/ADD_MONTHS or a date variable and n is a number, become `d + interval '1 day' * n`.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-017.

### O2PG-CV-040: TO_DATE

`TO_DATE(s, fmt)` becomes `to_timestamp(s, fmt)::timestamp(0)`, because PostgreSQL's to_date drops the time of day.

**Check:** Most format elements match; check RR, FF and NLS-dependent elements.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-012.

### O2PG-CV-041: One-argument TO_CHAR and TO_NUMBER

`TO_CHAR(x)` becomes `CAST(x AS text)` and `TO_NUMBER(x)` becomes `CAST(x AS numeric)`; PostgreSQL's versions need a format argument.

**Check:** TO_CHAR of a DATE used NLS_DATE_FORMAT in Oracle; the cast gives ISO format.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-012.

### O2PG-CV-042: DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR and GETLENGTH

`DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(lob, amount, offset)` becomes `substr(lob, offset, amount)` (note the argument order) and `DBMS_LOB.GETLENGTH(lob)` becomes `length(lob)`.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-008.

### O2PG-CV-043: DBMS_LOCK.SLEEP

`DBMS_LOCK.SLEEP(n);` and `DBMS_SESSION.SLEEP(n);` become `PERFORM pg_sleep(n);`.

### O2PG-CV-044: SYS_GUID

`SYS_GUID()` becomes `gen_random_uuid()` (core PostgreSQL 13+).

**Check:** SYS_GUID returns RAW(16); gen_random_uuid returns uuid.

### O2PG-CV-045: Two-argument INSTR

`INSTR(s, sub)` becomes `strpos(s, sub)`.

### O2PG-CV-046: MINUS

The `MINUS` set operator becomes `EXCEPT`.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-010.

### O2PG-CV-047: MERGE target aliases in UPDATE SET

In `MERGE INTO t a ... UPDATE SET a.col = ...`, the alias is removed from the SET targets; PostgreSQL does not allow qualified target columns.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-006.

### O2PG-CV-048: INSERT ... VALUES record

`INSERT INTO t VALUES rec;` becomes `INSERT INTO t VALUES (rec.*);`.

### O2PG-CV-049: Quoted identifiers

Quoted identifiers such as `"EMPLOYEES"` are folded the same way as `o2pg map-types` folds table and column names (lower case, quoted only when needed).

Related assessment rules: O2PG-OB-016.

### O2PG-CV-050: Alternative quoting and N'' literals

`q'[it's]'` becomes `'it''s'` and `N'text'` becomes `'text'`.

### O2PG-CV-051: Nested comment openers

A `/*` inside a block comment becomes `/ *`. PostgreSQL nests block comments; Oracle does not.

### O2PG-CV-052: SUBSTR from position 0

`SUBSTR(s, 0, n)` becomes `substr(s, 1, n)`. Oracle treats position 0 as 1; PostgreSQL would return one character less.

### O2PG-CV-053: Two-argument REPLACE

`REPLACE(s, x)` becomes `replace(s, x, '')`; Oracle's two-argument form removes x.

## Review points

### O2PG-RV-001: Object type not converted

*blocking*

this object is not converted (see the reason); the original source is kept below as a comment.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-OB-005, O2PG-OB-006, O2PG-OB-012, O2PG-PL-015.

### O2PG-RV-002: Autonomous transaction

*blocking*

PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION has no PostgreSQL equivalent; pg_background is not available on Azure Flexible Server and a postgres_fdw/dblink loopback is a workaround with its own costs. Prefer a redesign (log after the transaction, RAISE LOG, or the application).

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-003.

### O2PG-RV-003: BULK COLLECT

*blocking*

BULK COLLECT has no PL/pgSQL equivalent; use SELECT array_agg(col) INTO arr, a cursor loop, or better a single set-based statement.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-004.

### O2PG-RV-004: FORALL

*blocking*

FORALL has no PL/pgSQL equivalent; replace the loop with one set-based statement, e.g. UPDATE ... FROM unnest(arr) or INSERT ... SELECT.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-004.

### O2PG-RV-005: ROWNUM

*blocking*

ROWNUM has no PostgreSQL equivalent; use LIMIT (or FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY) for top-n and row_number() OVER (...) for numbering.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-002.

### O2PG-RV-006: CONNECT BY

*blocking*

hierarchical query: rewrite CONNECT BY / START WITH / PRIOR / LEVEL as WITH RECURSIVE.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-001.

### O2PG-RV-007: Oracle outer join operator

*blocking*

the (+) outer join operator does not exist in PostgreSQL; rewrite as LEFT/RIGHT JOIN.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-005.

### O2PG-RV-008: Pipelined functions

*blocking*

PIPELINED / PIPE ROW: rewrite as RETURNS SETOF (or RETURNS TABLE) with RETURN NEXT.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-016.

### O2PG-RV-009: Collection and record types

*blocking*

PL/SQL collection, record or subtype declaration: use a PostgreSQL array, a composite type (CREATE TYPE) or a temporary table.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-018, O2PG-OB-012.

### O2PG-RV-010: Data type with no mapping

*blocking*

no automatic mapping for this data type.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-DT-017.

### O2PG-RV-011: Package state

*blocking*

package-level variable: PostgreSQL has no package state; keep it in a table or temporary table, or in a custom setting via set_config()/current_setting().

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-002.

### O2PG-RV-012: User-defined exceptions

*blocking*

user-defined exception: PL/pgSQL cannot declare exceptions; RAISE a custom SQLSTATE (e.g. RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'U0001') and catch WHEN SQLSTATE 'U0001'.

### O2PG-RV-013: Other PRAGMA

*blocking*

PRAGMA has no PL/pgSQL equivalent (EXCEPTION_INIT: catch the matching SQLSTATE instead).

### O2PG-RV-014: Oracle-supplied package

*blocking*

Oracle-supplied package call with no direct PostgreSQL equivalent.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-008, O2PG-PL-009, O2PG-PL-010, O2PG-PL-011, O2PG-PL-012, O2PG-AZ-003.

### O2PG-RV-015: Oracle-only function

*blocking*

Oracle-only function with no PostgreSQL built-in (orafce provides some of them on Azure).

Related assessment rules: O2PG-AZ-005, O2PG-SQ-011, O2PG-SQ-015.

### O2PG-RV-016: Transaction control in a function or trigger

*blocking*

COMMIT/ROLLBACK is not allowed in a PostgreSQL function or trigger; move transaction control to the caller or make this a procedure.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-014.

### O2PG-RV-017: Savepoints and SET TRANSACTION

*blocking*

PL/pgSQL has no SAVEPOINT or SET TRANSACTION statement; use a nested BEGIN ... EXCEPTION block for partial rollback.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-014.

### O2PG-RV-018: GOTO

*blocking*

PL/pgSQL has no GOTO; restructure with loops, EXIT/CONTINUE and labels.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-017.

### O2PG-RV-019: Nested subprograms

*blocking*

nested procedure or function: PL/pgSQL cannot declare subprograms inside a block; move it to its own routine.

### O2PG-RV-020: Package initialisation section

*blocking*

package initialisation block: there is no package load event in PostgreSQL; run this explicitly where the state is first needed.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-002.

### O2PG-RV-021: Cursor attribute without a direct equivalent

*blocking*

cursor attribute with no direct equivalent: use GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT after the statement, or track the count yourself.

### O2PG-RV-022: DECODE that needs a hand-written CASE

*blocking*

DECODE with a non-literal search value on a complex expression: write the CASE by hand so the expression is evaluated once and NULLs still match.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-003.

### O2PG-RV-023: UPDATING('column')

*blocking*

UPDATING('col') has no TG_OP equivalent; use an UPDATE OF col trigger or compare NEW.col IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.col (which is not quite the same).

### O2PG-RV-024: Function with OUT parameters

*blocking*

a PostgreSQL function cannot have OUT parameters and a separate RETURN value; return a composite or make it a procedure.

### O2PG-RV-025: Parameter default order

*blocking*

PostgreSQL requires every parameter after one with a DEFAULT to have a default too; reorder the parameters and update named-notation callers.

### O2PG-RV-026: ROWID

*blocking*

ROWID has no stable PostgreSQL equivalent; use the primary key.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-DT-013.

### O2PG-RV-027: Flashback query

*blocking*

AS OF TIMESTAMP/SCN flashback queries have no PostgreSQL equivalent.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-016.

### O2PG-RV-028: DUAL left in place

*blocking*

this reference to DUAL could not be removed mechanically.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-009.

### O2PG-RV-029: Unsupported routine or trigger form

*blocking*

this routine or trigger form is not converted.

### O2PG-RV-030: Negative SUBSTR position

*blocking*

a negative SUBSTR position counts from the end in Oracle but not in PostgreSQL; use right() or compute the position.

### O2PG-RV-031: MERGE needs a check

*non-blocking*

MERGE runs on PostgreSQL 15+ (Azure Flexible Server offers 15, 16 and 17); check the ON condition, and that concurrent inserts are handled (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT may fit better).

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-006.

### O2PG-RV-032: MERGE with conditional UPDATE or DELETE

*blocking*

Oracle's UPDATE ... WHERE / DELETE WHERE inside MERGE: move the condition to WHEN MATCHED AND cond THEN UPDATE / DELETE.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-006.

### O2PG-RV-033: Dynamic SQL

*non-blocking*

dynamic SQL: the SQL text is not converted; check it is valid PostgreSQL and change :name binds to $1, $2 with USING.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-007.

### O2PG-RV-034: Empty string literal

*non-blocking*

'' is NULL in Oracle but an empty string in PostgreSQL; comparisons with '' and assignments of '' behave differently.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-008.

### O2PG-RV-035: Concatenation with possible NULLs

*non-blocking*

|| returns NULL in PostgreSQL when any operand is NULL; Oracle treats NULL as ''. Use concat() or COALESCE where an operand can be NULL.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-018.

### O2PG-RV-036: SQLCODE values

*non-blocking*

SQLSTATE is a five-character code such as 'P0002', not a negative number; check comparisons and anything that stores it.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-PL-013.

### O2PG-RV-037: SQLERRM with an argument

*non-blocking*

SQLERRM(code) does not exist in PL/pgSQL; SQLERRM only reports the current error.

### O2PG-RV-038: TRUNC of unknown type

*non-blocking*

TRUNC on a value of unknown type: PostgreSQL's trunc() is numeric only; use date_trunc('day', x) if x is a date or timestamp.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-011.

### O2PG-RV-039: Date arithmetic to check

*non-blocking*

date arithmetic: timestamp - timestamp is an interval in PostgreSQL (a number of days in Oracle), and timestamp +/- number needs interval '1 day' * n.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-017.

### O2PG-RV-040: Integer division

*non-blocking*

both operands look like integers: PostgreSQL truncates integer division (7/2 = 3), Oracle does not (3.5); cast one side to numeric.

### O2PG-RV-041: LEAST and GREATEST with NULLs

*non-blocking*

LEAST/GREATEST ignore NULL arguments in PostgreSQL; Oracle returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

### O2PG-RV-042: Regular expression functions

*non-blocking*

REGEXP_REPLACE replaces every match in Oracle but only the first in PostgreSQL unless the 'g' flag is given; check flags and the PostgreSQL 15+ regexp_* signatures.

### O2PG-RV-043: Single-argument TO_DATE

*blocking*

TO_DATE without a format relied on NLS_DATE_FORMAT; add an explicit format.

Related assessment rules: O2PG-SQ-012.

### O2PG-RV-044: Three- and four-argument INSTR

*blocking*

INSTR with a start position or occurrence has no PostgreSQL built-in (orafce has instr).
